title: MASTER SOC INVESTIGATION

theory.concept: This is the final assessment. A new intrusion is unfolding across Northwind Logistics and you are the lead analyst. Everything the previous twenty-nine cases taught you applies at once: triage, authentication analysis, endpoint and Linux investigation, network and DNS analysis, malware indicators, threat intelligence, persistence hunting, privilege escalation, lateral movement, C2 characterisation, exfiltration quantification, SIEM correlation, ATT&CK mapping, incident response sequencing and forensics. No panel here tells you which events matter.
theory.why: A SOC analyst is judged on whether they can carry an incident end to end under time pressure, distinguish the intrusion from the noise around it, and produce a report that survives review by an incident manager, a lawyer and a regulator.
look: Work the phases in order but re-read earlier evidence as later phases change its meaning
Every phase contains at least one benign event designed to look malicious
Numbers matter: counts, intervals, volumes and timestamps all go into the report
Controls that worked are findings too
fp: Two of the alerts in the opening queue are not part of this incident
At least one administrative action during the window is authorised and ticketed
tips: Build the timeline as you go rather than at the end
Name the enabling weakness for every stage, not just the technique

case.alert: MASTER ASSESSMENT - Multi-stage enterprise intrusion, lead analyst assignment
case.brief: Three months after the TA-4411 incident, Northwind Logistics is intruded again by a different actor. You are the lead analyst with no Tier-2 support available until you produce your assessment. Investigate all ten phases, answer every question from evidence, construct the attack timeline, map the techniques, decide severity and containment, and write the full incident report. This assessment is not passed by opening it.

mitre: Full chain - to be mapped by the analyst

evidence.name: PHASE 10 - Response Context and Forensics
rows: Memory (SRV-ERP01, captured 15:10): injected RWX region in svchost.exe pid=1420; strings 'remote:nwx', 'metrics-sync-eu.net', rclone config with bearer token; connections 45.61.202.44:443 ESTABLISHED
Prefetch SRV-ERP01: MSUPD.EXE run_count=22 first=06-11 13:21 | RCLONE.EXE run_count=1 first=06-12 09:44 | LOCK.EXE: no entry
Shadow copies on SRV-ERP01 survived (deletion was executed on SRV-BKP01 only); staged CSVs recovered
Controls that worked: PCI segmentation denied svc_report2 (0xC000015B); EDR shadow-copy rule fired and was actioned; SRV-ERP01 shadow copies preserved evidence

Controls that failed: VPN firmware advisory NWV-2026-004 deferred (CHG-5088); MFA not enforced at identity provider for appliance-established sessions; svc_sqlreport password unchanged since 2021 with SPN registered (kerberoastable); no alert on RC4 ticket burst; no alert on vssadmin until impact stage

CTI: TTPs (edge appliance auth bypass, kerberoasting, rclone to commercial cloud, vssadmin deletion, GPO-deployed encryptor) match ransomware affiliate cluster TA-7730 (aka HOLLOWREEF). Typical sequence: access -> exfiltration -> encryption within 48-72h. Encryption had NOT yet occurred.

questions.label: PHASE 1 - Which two alerts in the opening queue are NOT part of this incident? (name both IDs)
questions.hint: One is a capacity event on a tier-3 asset; one maps to an approved change.

questions.label: PHASE 1 - Which alert should have been ranked highest, and on what basis?
questions.hint: Consider asset tier and what the rule actually describes happening on a domain controller.

questions.label: PHASE 2 - Attacker source IP
questions.hint: Present on the anomalous VPN authentication and the requests preceding it.

questions.label: PHASE 2 - What vulnerability was exploited on the VPN appliance? (name the advisory)
questions.hint: An advisory published on 06-02 was deferred rather than applied.

questions.label: PHASE 2 - What evidence shows the appliance was exploited rather than simply logged into with stolen credentials?
questions.hint: Look at the four HTTP requests four minutes before the successful authentication.

questions.label: PHASE 2 - Why did the identity provider record no MFA prompt for session SES-77120?
questions.hint: Read the identity provider note and the control-failure list.

questions.label: PHASE 3 - What is the full path of the first-stage implant?
questions.hint: One unsigned file is written to a roaming profile directory at 03:22.

questions.label: PHASE 3 - Which 09:02 event is legitimate, and why?
questions.hint: Compare its parent process and approval status with the attacker activity.

questions.label: PHASE 4 - How many Kerberos service tickets did the attacker request?
questions.hint: One ticket at 04:52:10 plus the burst that follows, corroborated by the exported file count.

questions.label: PHASE 4 - Name the credential-access technique
questions.hint: RC4 service tickets requested in bulk for accounts with SPNs, then exported for offline cracking.

questions.label: PHASE 4 - Which service account did the attacker crack and use, and what made it vulnerable?
questions.hint: One account has an SPN, a password set in 2021, and appears from a VPN address for the first time.

questions.label: PHASE 5 - Name the persistence mechanisms the attacker established (list at least three)
questions.hint: Count across SRV-SQL02, SRV-JUMP01 and SRV-ERP01 - a service, a scheduled task, a registry service entry and a new account.

questions.label: PHASE 5 - Which 7045 service installation is legitimate?
questions.hint: One service is signed by a vendor and covered by a change record.

questions.label: PHASE 6 - How many hosts did the attacker successfully reach after the jump server?
questions.hint: Count SQL02, ERP01 and BKP01 - one further destination was refused.

questions.label: PHASE 6 - Which host refused the movement and what does the sub-status mean?
questions.hint: The same sub-status code you saw in the lateral movement case.

questions.label: PHASE 7 - C2 domain and beacon interval in seconds
questions.hint: One destination carries a POST channel at a much longer cadence than the legitimate telemetry.

questions.label: PHASE 7 - What does the 02:00-06:00 silence on 06-12 indicate?
questions.hint: Implants with a fixed interval do not stop for four hours on their own.

questions.label: PHASE 8 - What tool was used for exfiltration and how much data left?
questions.hint: An unsigned utility dropped at 09:40 with a cloud-sync command line.

questions.label: PHASE 8 - Which large transfer in this phase is NOT exfiltration, and why?
questions.hint: One 400+ GB transfer has a change record, a fixed window and a contracted destination.

questions.label: PHASE 8 - How many customer records are in scope for notification?
questions.hint: Read the data classification line.

questions.label: PHASE 9 - What three actions show the attacker was preparing for ransomware deployment?
questions.hint: Destroy recovery options, weaken backups, and stage a way to run a payload everywhere at once.

questions.label: PHASE 9 - Was the encryption payload executed? State the artefact that proves your answer.
questions.hint: Check the prefetch evidence for lock.exe in Phase 10.

questions.label: PHASE 9 - What mechanism would have deployed the payload estate-wide?
questions.hint: One modification at 14:22 targets every workstation at once.

questions.label: PHASE 10 - Which actor cluster do the TTPs match?
questions.hint: Read the CTI line in Phase 10.

questions.label: PHASE 10 - Name two controls that worked
questions.hint: The Phase 10 panel lists three.

questions.label: PHASE 10 - Name the single control failure that enabled initial access
questions.hint: An advisory published nine days before the intrusion was deferred.

questions.label: ATT&CK - Technique ID for the Kerberos ticket abuse
questions.hint: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets, Kerberoasting sub-technique.

questions.label: ATT&CK - Technique ID for shadow copy deletion (inhibit system recovery)
questions.hint: Impact tactic, inhibiting recovery.

questions.label: ATT&CK - Technique ID for exfiltration to cloud storage
questions.hint: Exfiltration Over Web Service, cloud storage sub-technique.

questions.label: RESPONSE - What is the first action you order, and why?
questions.hint: Preservation precedes any action that destroys evidence - and one host is still holding live C2 state in memory.

questions.label: RESPONSE - Which credential must be treated as compromised estate-wide beyond the named accounts?
questions.hint: Kerberoasting exported 38 tickets, not one - every account in that export is a candidate.

questions.label: RESPONSE - Why must containment across all four hosts be simultaneous?
questions.hint: One host is controlled through an internal pipe relay, and the operator is a human who will react.

recommend.text: Capture memory from all four hosts, then isolate simultaneously; block 45.61.202.44 and both registered domains; disable svc_report2 (preserve, do not delete); rotate every service account exposed by the kerberoast export plus krbtgt; patch VPN-GW01 to 9.1.6; restore backup retention and validate backup integrity; notify legal and privacy for 12,400 customer records.

hints: Work phase by phase and resist judging any event until you have read the phase that follows it. Two alerts in the opening queue are noise, one large transfer in Phase 8 is a contracted backup, and one service installation in Phase 5 is a vendor agent.

The single most important judgement in this assessment is what the attacker had NOT yet done. Check the prefetch evidence for the payload in Phase 10, then read what the CTI line says about the actor's typical 48-72 hour sequence.
review: TA-7730 (HOLLOWREEF), a ransomware affiliate, entered through VPN-GW01 by exploiting NWV-2026-004 - an authentication bypass patched on 2 June and deferred under CHG-5088. The path traversal requests at 02:58:40 prove exploitation rather than simple credential use, and the identity provider recorded no MFA prompt because sessions established at the appliance never reached it. From the VPN pool the attacker took RDP to SRV-JUMP01, enumerated Active Directory, dropped msupd.exe, and kerberoasted 38 RC4 service tickets from DC-02 - an alert that fired at MEDIUM and was never worked. Cracking svc_sqlreport (SPN registered, password unchanged since 2021) gave local administrator rights on two servers, from which the attacker dumped LSASS, installed service and scheduled-task persistence, created svc_report2, and moved to SRV-ERP01 and the backup server via NTLM and WMI. SRV-PCI02 refused them with 0xC000015B - segmentation held again. C2 ran at 1800 seconds through a Let's Encrypt-certified, Cloudflare-fronted domain registered on 28 May, and the four-hour silence overnight reveals a human operator's working pattern. 3.9 GB of ERP exports (12,400 customer records) left via rclone to commercial cloud storage; the 408 GB DR replication in the same phase is contracted and unrelated. Then the decisive phase: shadow copies deleted on the backup server, Veeam retention cut from 30 days to 1, an encryptor staged as lock.exe, and a GPO startup script prepared to run it on every workstation. Prefetch proves lock.exe never executed. The EDR shadow-copy rule fired CRITICAL and was actioned within minutes - the first alert in this incident to receive an immediate response, and the reason Northwind was contained hours before encryption rather than days after it. Three controls worked; five failed. The organisational finding is the same one as three months ago: detections fired, and nobody owned the action.
